Debug tools act on the running process immediately. Misuse may break activation or authorization.
Official / custom manifest URLs, timeout, insecure links, latest build
Edit every writable variable in memory. No safety filter.
Tokens, interface states, identity, memory, process and config snapshots
Read and write every file in the app private storage
Wipe all app data and configuration, then exit
This clears all preferences, authorization records, private files and the database. Device owner / admin identity is kept.
The manager will exit immediately after wiping. Reopen it to rebuild defaults.
Variable names are shown as-is. Changes take effect immediately; some are restored on restart.
Tap any row to copy its value. Refresh to take a new snapshot.
CE and DE storage are both listed. Binary files are read-only; edits to api_policy.json / whitelist.json reload immediately.
Query the official server once each time the app opens. Only shows a card when a newer version exists.
NeoDhizuku module: lets selected apps use DeviceOwner APIs through NeoDhizuku. Do not enable the System Framework scope.
When off, the module does nothing even if loaded
Leave empty to follow the scope selected in LSPosed. Selected apps are checked below.
No apps are being taken over yet
Not working on a patched app?
The patched app needs to see NeoDhizuku. Copy the required setting below and add it while patching.
The module only works inside the apps you selected in LSPosed or patched with LSPatch. Devices without them are completely unaffected.

Remove or transfer a device admin component even when its package name was changed. Candidates come from the system, not from the current applicationId. Transfer requires this instance to be the device owner.
Decided by the framework. Nothing to select here.
After changing the selected apps in LSPosed / LSPatch, fully close and reopen those apps. The switches below apply immediately.
The module was just enabled. Reopen any target apps that are already running.
This unconditionally calls the clear device owner, clear profile owner and remove active admin APIs. If this app is still the owner, it must be activated again. This cannot be undone.
Removing or transferring a device admin / owner identity cannot be undone. Check the component below before continuing.

The framework scope (apps selected in LSPosed, or apps patched by LSPatch) decides which processes the module is injected into. This list decides which of them are actually taken over. Both layers must match. Leave it empty to follow the framework.
Changes here take effect the next time that process starts. Force-stop and reopen the target app.
Let apps read the list of active administrators
Forward device policy requests from apps to NeoDhizuku
More advanced options are on the Debug pages.
Pretend the module is active even when it is not (not recommended)
Let apps use features that normally require device owner
Let apps install or uninstall packages silently
Let apps see the real device owner
Transferring the device owner inside NeoDhizuku always requires two confirmation dialogs. The switch above only affects third-party apps.
This transfers the device owner to NeoDhizuku through Dhizuku. This action is irreversible.
The transfer will run immediately. If the current owner is not active, activation will fail.
Frosted-glass blur behind cards when a custom background is set.
Switch the look of the app. Takes effect immediately
When off, the navigation bar sits flush against the screen edge and marks the current page with color only

Device owner will be transferred to the app below. This app loses device owner rights immediately and the change cannot be undone. If the target app has no authorization entry, ownership may be unrecoverable. Check the app name and package name carefully.
Confirm again: the transfer cannot be undone inside NeoDhizuku. Check the app below once more.
